data.long_meaning: The name Karunesh is derived from the Sanskrit words 'karuna' meaning compassion, and 'ish' meaning Lord. The name is bestowed upon a child to instill in them the qualities of compassion and mercy. The name Karunesh carries the meaning “Compassionate, Merciful” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Karunesh usually hope their child will grow to embody compassionate, merciful and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: May you radiate compassion and mercy to all.
data.etymology: Karunesh belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Compassionate, Merciful.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Karunesh total 7, giving a life-path number of 7. Number 7 is linked with Ketu and with the qualities of reflection, wisdom and inner depth.

Hinduism emphasizes the importance of caring for others, showing kindness, and treating all living beings with respect and dignity. The name serves as a constant reminder for the bearer to uphold these values and contribute positively to their community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Karunesh represents the divine quality of love and compassion belonging to the Hindu deity, Lord Shiva. The name invokes the blessings of Lord Shiva, who is known as the embodiment of mercy, compassion, and forgiveness. By carrying this name, one is believed to be protected and blessed by the divine energies of this powerful deity.

historical_references.reference: Karunesh was a renowned Indian musician and spiritual teacher who popularized the esoteric Indian classical music genre called 'Gayan Sampradaya'. This tradition evolved around the 12th century AD in the Hindu temple towns of South India, focusing on the development of an advanced vocal technique called 'Gayan' or 'Gayaki'. The Gayan Sampradaya emphasized a deep emotional connection between the musician and the divine, with the performance meant to be a spiritual experience for both the artist and the audience.
historical_references.context: Evolution and popularization of the Gayan Sampradaya music tradition in South India

historical_references.reference: Karunesh, born as Krishna Murthy in 1950 in Mysore, India, was a disciple of the renowned Indian classical music maestro Mysore T. Chowdiah. He adopted the name 'Karunesh' during his spiritual journey and started performing and teaching the Gayan Sampradaya tradition in the late 1980s. He is known to have revived and propagated this ancient tradition, which had been on the brink of extinction.
